questions.explain: Clock times take *at*.
Days and dates take *on*.
Seasons, months and years take *in*.
No preposition before *next, last, this, every*.

questions.q: What time did you arrive *___* the airport?
questions.explain: *arrive at* a building or point; *arrive in* a city or country; never *arrive to*.
We are *on* buses, trains and planes, but *in* cars and taxis.

questions.q: He was born *___* a small village in Wales.
questions.explain: Towns, villages and countries take *in*.
*during* + noun tells us when; *while* needs a clause.

questions.q: Please send the report *___* Friday at the latest.
questions.explain: *by* = not later than (a deadline); *until* = continuing up to a time.
*by* + means of transport, with no article. But *on foot*.

questions.q: *___* the bad weather, the match went ahead.
questions.explain: *in spite of* / *despite* (no *of*) + noun. *Although* needs a clause.
Here *to* is a preposition, so it is followed by *-ing*.
*good at* + noun or *-ing*.
*onto* shows movement to a surface.

questions.q: I went to the shop *___* some bread.
questions.explain: A person's purpose is expressed with the *to*-infinitive.
*for + -ing* describes the function of an object.

questions.q: Children *___* 12 must be with an adult.
questions.explain: *under* is used for ages and amounts below a number.

questions.q: We had lunch and *___* we went to the museum.
questions.explain: As an adverb on its own, use *afterwards* (or *after that*), not *after*.
Prepositions are followed by *-ing*: *without saying*.

questions.q: The house is *___* the river, just a few metres away.
questions.explain: *by* can mean *next to*: *a house by the river*.
*as* + noun = in the role of.
*explain something to someone*: the person needs *to*.
*wait for* someone; the preposition goes at the end of the question.

questions.q: There were *___* a hundred people at the meeting.
questions.explain: *over* = more than, with numbers.
*within* = before the end of a period.
